findings.summary: The landing line still reports five tests and a 2-of-5 negative control while the head carries nine tests and a 5-of-9 control at b4954b211, and promotion comments this line onto the plan section, so the plan would record a weaker gate than the code carries.

The first test_logs entry /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/r-20261027T090436433416-nonfinite-refusal/nfr/test.log records five tests at base revision d3dcd9ce3 and no persisted green nine-test log exists; the nine-test head result lives only in the worker transcript, while I re-ran the file at cb0fc40fe and got 9 passed with EXIT=0.

The reduced-Newton production-mask test defines its own moment_finiteness that ignores the state arguments and fabricates a NaN CellCurrentMoments, so the production closure at nova/equilibrium/reduced_newton.py:1034 and its _current_moments derivation stay unexercised; the certificate side is now genuinely on the production closure at scripts/prototypes/fast_map_production/solver.py:160.

The terminal-step asymmetry the gained commit fixes in the certificate driver remains here: the mask is read only at the head of each trip, so a non-finite moment produced only by the final trip's newton or boundary step reaches the returned state unrefused, and the new tests do not reach that path because the refusal fires on trip entry.

The row gate's per-arm import is not evidenced by the log header: row-cli-gate.sh:51 prints nova.__file__ from the launcher environment, so both arms report the reviewed worktree's path, though the child receives PYTHONPATH set to its own tree and each arm regenerated its own part receipt.
